en: to put things away in order

examples.ko: 가을에 수확한 고구마를 잘 갈무리해 두었어요.
examples.en: I stored the sweet potatoes I harvested in the fall properly.
I took some time to wrap up this year's work.
I wrapped up the trip by organizing the photos.
Store the grain in a place without moisture.
I'll wrap up this task today.
To finish a piece of writing well, the conclusion is important.

explain: 물건을 잘 간수해 둘 때도, 일이나 글을 깔끔하게 끝낼 때도 써요. 일상에서는 '정리하다', '마무리하다'를 더 많이 말해서 '갈무리하다'는 조금 정성스럽고 글 같은 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I stored the kimchi away carefully.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 두다'를 붙여 나중을 위해 잘 간수해 놓는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-아/어 두다' it means putting something away carefully for later.

phrases.example: 한 해를 갈무리하고 나서 새 계획을 세워요.
phrases.en: After wrapping up the year, I make new plans.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일을 깔끔하게 끝낸 다음 다른 일을 이어서 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when finishing something neatly before moving on to the next thing.

phrases.en: I put the papers on my desk in order.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이나 일을 가지런히 하는 뜻의 쉬운 말이라 일상에서 '갈무리하다' 대신 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word for putting things or tasks in order, used in daily speech instead of 갈무리하다.

explain_en: It is used both for putting things away safely and for finishing a task or piece of writing neatly. In daily speech people tend to say '정리하다' or '마무리하다', so '갈무리하다' sounds a bit careful and written.

examples.en: I record my day in a diary every day.
I wrote down the lesson in my notebook.
If you write it down right away, it's easy to remember later.
I want to record what happened on the trip.

examples.ko: 저는 모든 일을 기록하는 습관이 있어요.
examples.en: I have a habit of recording everything.

examples.ko: 어제 기록한 내용을 지금 읽어 볼게요.
examples.en: I'll read the notes I recorded yesterday now.

explain: '적다'는 가볍게 메모할 때, '기록하다'는 남겨 두려고 정리해서 쓸 때 써요. 사진이나 영상으로 남기는 것도 '기록하다'라고 해요. 명사 '기록'은 스포츠에서 '신기록'처럼도 쓰여요.

phrases.en: I write down what the teacher says in my notebook.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가볍게 메모할 때는 '기록하다'보다 '적다'가 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: For quick notes, 적다 is more natural than 기록하다.

phrases.example: 여행에서 있었던 일을 공책에 기록으로 남겼어요.
phrases.en: I kept a record of what happened on the trip in my notebook.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나중에 볼 수 있게 남겨 둔다는 뜻을 더 분명하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Makes clearer that you are keeping something to look back on later.

phrases.en: I record each day with photos.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글이 아니라 사진으로 남길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when recording with photos instead of writing.

explain_en: '적다' is for jotting something down lightly; '기록하다' is for writing it up so it is kept. Saving something in photos or video is also '기록하다'. The noun '기록' appears in sports too, as in '신기록' (new record).

gh: capture sound or voice on a device

p.n: 녹음하다 means you capture the meeting as audio instead of writing it down.

t90.ax: I record my day in a diary every day.

examples.en: I left the phone number out of the application.

examples.ko: 메일에 첨부 파일을 누락하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not leave out the attachment in the email.

examples.ko: 제 이름을 누락한 채로 명단이 나왔어요.
examples.en: The list came out with my name omitted.

examples.ko: 중요한 내용을 누락하지 않았는지 다시 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: Check again that you have not left out anything important.
I am sorry I omitted one thing from the minutes.

examples.ko: 한 줄을 누락할 때가 많아서 꼼꼼히 봐야 해요.
examples.en: I often skip a line, so I have to check carefully.

explain: 일상에서는 '빠뜨리다'를 많이 쓰고, 누락하다는 서류·명단·기록에서 빠진 경우에 써요. 빠진 쪽을 주어로 하면 '누락되다'가 돼요.

phrases.en: My name was left out of the list.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빠진 것을 주어로 할 때 써요. 누구 잘못인지 말하지 않고 빠졌다는 사실만 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the omitted thing as the subject; it states the fact without blaming anyone.

phrases.en: Please check that nothing is missing from the documents.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류나 목록을 확인할 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often used when checking documents or lists.

phrases.en: I left out one number.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 더 많이 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요. 누락하다는 글이나 공식적인 자리에 더 알맞아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easier everyday word; 누락하다 fits writing and formal settings better.

explain_en: In daily talk Koreans say '빠뜨리다'; 누락하다 is for things missing from documents, lists, or records. If the missing thing is the subject, use '누락되다'.

examples.en: The judges select the book of the year.
The school selected a representative student.
It took time to choose the venue.
We will contact the people we selected.
I want to select just one candidate.

examples.ko: 기준에 맞는 곳을 선정해서 보내 주세요.
examples.en: Please pick places that fit the criteria and send them.

explain: '고르다'는 일상에서 쓰고, '선정하다'는 기준을 세워 공식적으로 뽑을 때 써요. 상, 대회, 공모, 이벤트 결과에서 자주 나와요. 뽑힌 쪽에서는 '선정되다'를 써요.

phrases.en: My picture was selected in the contest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뽑힌 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the one who was chosen.

phrases.en: Please tell me the selection criteria.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇을 보고 뽑는지 물을 때 쓰는 명사 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun pairing used to ask what is considered in choosing.

phrases.en: Our class chooses a class president.
phrases.nuance_ko: '선정하다'보다 쉽고 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 선정하다 and more common in daily life.

explain_en: The everyday word for choosing is used casually, while this one fits picking by criteria in an official way, as in awards, contests and event results. The passive form is what the chosen side says.

dis.h: choose after review; prizes, sites, winners
gh: pick via exam or competition; team, staff
pick from many for a key role
screen and sort out by quality

p.n: 선발하다 implies picking through a test or competition; 선정하다 is a general choice.

t90.ax: It took time to choose the venue.

examples.ko: 회의 속기록은 누구나 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: Anyone can read the transcript of the meeting.
I found that remark in the National Assembly transcript.
After reading the transcript, I found the mood was different.
The trial transcript was released and became a hot topic.

examples.ko: 사고 경위를 속기록으로 확인할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can check how the accident happened in the transcript.
I confirmed the exact remarks based on the transcript.

explain: '회의록'은 회의 내용을 정리한 기록이고, '속기록'은 말한 것을 빠짐없이 그대로 받아 적은 기록이라는 점이 달라요. 국회, 법원 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: We keep the meeting content as a stenographic record.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말한 내용을 그대로 기록으로 만들어 둔다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to preserve what was said as a word-for-word record.

phrases.en: The National Assembly released the transcript.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기록을 누구나 볼 수 있게 한다는 뜻으로 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means making the record available to the public, common in news.

phrases.example: 속기록을 확인해 보면 알 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can find out by checking the transcript.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누가 무슨 말을 했는지 정확히 알아보려고 기록을 살펴볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when looking at the record to see exactly who said what.

explain_en: '회의록' is a summarized record of a meeting, while '속기록' is a transcript written down just as it was spoken. It often appears in news about the National Assembly and courts.

examples.ko: 오늘 졸업식 식순을 미리 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me today's graduation ceremony program in advance.
Following the program, we will start with the pledge to the flag.
The program changed, so the congratulatory speech comes first.
They handed out the event program sheet at the entrance.
The host is running the event while looking at the program.
Wouldn't it be boring if the program is too long?

explain: '순서'는 어떤 일에든 쓰지만 '식순'은 졸업식, 개회식 같은 공식 행사의 진행 순서에만 써요. '식순에 따라', '식순을 짜다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: According to the program, we will begin with the opening remarks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정해진 행사 순서대로 진행한다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that a ceremony proceeds in its set order.

phrases.en: The teachers planned the program for the entrance ceremony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사의 진행 순서를 계획해서 정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when planning and setting the order of a ceremony.

phrases.en: I checked the program before the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 진행 순서를 미리 살펴볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when looking over the order of events in advance.

explain_en: '순서' (order) can be used for anything, but '식순' is only for the running order of formal ceremonies such as graduations or opening events. You will hear it in phrases like '식순에 따라' and '식순을 짜다'.

t90.ax: Wouldn't it be boring if the program is too long?

en: to end; to finish; to wrap up

examples.ko: 저는 다 쓰고 나면 앱을 바로 종료해요.
examples.en: When I'm done, I close the app right away.
We ended the meeting early.
Press this button to close the program.
Be sure to save before you quit the game.
It's time to end the class.
Close it and then turn it back on.

explain: 끝내는 사람이 있으면 '종료하다', 저절로 끝나면 '종료되다'예요. 컴퓨터나 앱을 끌 때도 써요. 일상에서는 '끝내다'를 더 편하게 써요.

phrases.example: 저는 일을 빨리 끝내고 집에 갔어요.
phrases.en: I finished my work quickly and went home.
phrases.nuance_ko: '종료하다'보다 쉽고 일상에서 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and more casual than '종료하다' in daily life.

phrases.en: I close the program before turning off the computer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 컴퓨터에서 프로그램을 끌 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when closing a program on a computer.

phrases.example: 시간이 다 됐으니 회의를 종료해 주세요.
phrases.en: Time is up, so please end the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끝내 달라고 정중하게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to politely ask someone to end something.

explain_en: If someone ends it, use '종료하다'; if it ends on its own, '종료되다'. You also use it to close a computer or app. In daily talk, '끝내다' is the easier word.

dis.h: formal: someone ends or shuts something
gh: wrap up a task with final touches
formal: concludes a case or war

p.n: 마무리하다 means wrapping up the final parts; 종료하다 just ends it officially.

examples.en: Many scholars took part in compiling the dictionary.

examples.ko: 이 책은 십 년에 걸친 편찬 작업 끝에 나왔어요.
examples.en: This book came out after ten years of compilation work.
The compilation of the history book began on the king's order.

examples.ko: 교과서 편찬 과정을 다룬 다큐를 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched a documentary about how textbooks are compiled.

examples.ko: 편찬을 맡은 선생님이 마지막 확인을 하고 있어요.
examples.en: The teacher in charge of the compilation is doing the final check.

examples.ko: 새 백과사전의 편찬이 곧 끝날 예정이에요.
examples.en: The compilation of the new encyclopedia is due to finish soon.

explain: 혼자 쓰기보다 '사전 편찬', '편찬 작업'처럼 책을 만드는 일과 함께 나와요. 동사는 '편찬하다'이고, 일상에서는 '엮다'나 '만들다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: He is a member of the dictionary compilation committee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책을 엮는 일에 참여하는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a person who takes part in compiling a book.

phrases.example: 역사책 편찬을 위해 옛 자료를 모았어요.
phrases.en: We gathered old materials to compile a history book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책 종류 뒤에 붙여 어떤 책을 만드는 일인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Added after a book type to say what kind of book is being compiled.

phrases.en: Scholars compiled the textbook.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '편찬'의 동사형으로 문장에서 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of '편찬', used when describing the action in a sentence.

explain_en: It rarely stands alone and usually appears with book-making, as in '사전 편찬' or '편찬 작업'. The verb is '편찬하다', and in daily speech people also say '엮다' or '만들다'.

examples.en: I took charge of writing the minutes.

examples.ko: 회의록에는 계약이 취소된 경위가 간단히 적혀 있었어요.
examples.en: The minutes briefly described how the contract came to be canceled.

examples.ko: 회의가 끝나면 회의록을 팀원들에게 메일로 보내 주세요.
examples.en: When the meeting ends, please email the minutes to the team.
Could you look up the last meeting's minutes for me?

examples.ko: 회의록이 아직 안 올라왔는데 언제 올라와요?
examples.en: The minutes haven't been posted yet. When will they be up?

examples.ko: 회의록 끝에 다음 회의 날짜도 적어 두었어요.
examples.en: I also wrote the next meeting date at the end of the minutes.

explain: 보통 '회의록을 작성하다', '회의록을 쓰다'처럼 말해요. 회사나 학교에서 회의가 끝난 뒤 공유하는 문서를 가리켜서 일상 대화보다는 업무 이야기에서 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: I'll write today's minutes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '작성하다'보다 쉬운 말로, 회의 내용을 글로 정리할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler way to say 'to draw up' the minutes; used when writing up what was discussed.

phrases.en: After the meeting, I sent the minutes to the team.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회의 후에 문서를 공유하는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for sharing the document with others after a meeting.

phrases.en: Please write down the decisions in the minutes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회의록 안에 어떤 내용을 넣는다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when saying what content goes into the minutes.

explain_en: It usually appears as '회의록을 작성하다' or '회의록을 쓰다'. It refers to the document shared after a meeting at work or school, so it comes up more in work talk than in casual conversation.

examples.en: This international competition is held every other year.

examples.ko: 우리 학교 축제는 격년제라서 올해는 없어요.
examples.en: Our school festival is held every other year, so there isn't one this year.
It's a biennial event, so it won't be held next year.

examples.ko: 박람회를 격년제에서 매년 하는 것으로 바꿨어요.
examples.en: They changed the fair from every other year to every year.

examples.ko: 이 상은 격년제여서 이 년에 한 번 줘요.
examples.en: This prize is biennial, so it's given once every two years.
Some companies have health checkups every other year.

explain: '격년'은 한 해를 거른다는 뜻이라, 격년제는 이 년에 한 번 하는 방식이에요. '격년제로 열리다/하다/운영하다'처럼 써요. 반대로 매년 하는 건 '매년'이고, 하루 걸러 하는 건 '격일제'예요.

phrases.en: This competition is held every other year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제도 이름보다 한 해 걸러 하는 주기를 말해서 '격년제로'보다 가볍게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes the every-other-year cycle rather than naming a system, so it sounds lighter than 격년제로.

phrases.example: 우리 가족은 2년에 한 번 해외여행을 가요.
phrases.en: My family travels abroad once every two years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '격년제' 대신 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday talk, people say this instead of 격년제.

phrases.en: This award is run on a biennial basis.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사나 제도를 운영하는 방식을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about how an event or system is run.

explain_en: '격년' means skipping a year, so '격년제' is a system of doing something once every two years. It is used as '격년제로 열리다/하다/운영하다'. Doing it every year is '매년', and every other day is '격일제'.

examples.ko: 이 문학 잡지는 계간지라서 석 달에 한 번 나와요.
examples.en: This literary magazine is a quarterly, so it comes out once every three months.
I borrowed the latest issue of the quarterly from the library.

examples.ko: 저는 매 분기 계간지에 글을 써요.
examples.en: I write for the quarterly every quarter.
Quarterlies tend to have deeper content than monthlies.

examples.ko: 이번 가을호 계간지가 아직 안 왔어요.
examples.en: This fall issue of the quarterly hasn't arrived yet.
That poet made a debut through a well-known quarterly.

explain: '주간지', '월간지'와 같이 발행 간격으로 잡지를 나누는 말이에요. 계간지는 계절마다 나와서 '봄호', '가을호'처럼 부르는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.example: 계간 잡지는 일 년에 네 번 나와요.
phrases.en: A quarterly magazine comes out four times a year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '계간지'를 풀어서 말한 것으로, '계간'은 계절마다 나온다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A spelled-out version of 계간지; 계간 means issued every season.

phrases.en: I subscribe to a literary quarterly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정해진 기간마다 받아 보려고 신청하는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means signing up to receive it regularly.

phrases.en: My writing was published in the winter issue of the quarterly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계간지는 '봄호, 여름호, 가을호, 겨울호'처럼 계절로 호를 불러요.
phrases.nuance_en: Quarterlies name their issues by season, like spring or winter issue.

explain_en: Like '주간지' (weekly) and '월간지' (monthly), it names a magazine by its publishing interval. Quarterlies come out each season, so they are often called things like '봄호' (spring issue) or '가을호' (fall issue).

examples.en: The company decided to put the criteria for working from home in writing.
The union demanded that the vacation rules be put in writing.

examples.ko: 규칙을 명문화하면 불필요한 분쟁을 줄일 수 있어요.
examples.en: Putting rules in writing can reduce unnecessary disputes.

examples.ko: 구두 약속은 나중에 문제가 되니 명문화해 두세요.
examples.en: Verbal promises can become a problem later, so put them in writing.

examples.ko: 명문화한 지침이 있어서 직원들이 덜 헷갈려요.
examples.en: Because there are written guidelines, employees get less confused.
We put the agreed contents into the contract in writing.

explain: 말로만 정해 둔 규칙이나 약속을 문서에 분명히 적어 두는 것이에요. '규정을 명문화하다', '계약서에 명문화하다'처럼 규정, 약속, 지침이 목적어로 자주 와요. 일상에서는 '문서로 남기다', '글로 적어 두다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: What was decided at the meeting was put in writing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 규칙이 문서로 정리되었다고 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say a rule has been put into a document.

phrases.en: Be sure to keep the agreement in a document.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 '명문화하다' 대신 쉽게 쓸 수 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday alternative to '명문화하다'.

phrases.en: There is no written regulation, so it's confusing.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ'으로 규정을 꾸며서 글로 정해진 규칙을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It modifies a regulation to mean one that has been set in writing.

explain_en: It means writing down rules or promises that were only set verbally so they are clear in a document. Rules, promises and guidelines often serve as the object, as in '규정을 명문화하다' or '계약서에 명문화하다'. In daily talk people also say '문서로 남기다' or '글로 적어 두다'.

examples.en: I heard a closed-door meeting was held somewhere in Seoul.

examples.ko: 친구가 지방 모처에 있는 회사에 취직했대요.
examples.en: My friend got a job at a company somewhere in the provinces.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 모처의 한 아파트에 불이 났다고 했어요.
examples.en: The news said a fire broke out in an apartment somewhere.

examples.ko: 모처로 오라는 문자를 받았는데 주소가 없어요.
examples.en: I got a text telling me to come to a certain place, but there's no address.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 도심 모처 카페에서 만났다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the two met at a cafe somewhere downtown.

examples.ko: 비밀 장소라서 모처라고만 말할 수 있어요.
examples.en: It's a secret place, so I can only say it's somewhere.

explain: '모처럼(오랜만에)'과 헷갈리기 쉽지만 전혀 다른 말이에요. 모처는 정확한 장소를 밝히지 않을 때 '서울 모처'처럼 쓰고, 주로 뉴스나 글에서 나와요. 말할 때는 '어딘가'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I heard the two of them met somewhere in Seoul.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지역 이름 뒤에 붙여서 정확한 장소는 밝히지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed after a place name when the exact location isn't disclosed.

phrases.en: They held a secret meeting at an undisclosed location.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '-에서'를 붙인 모양으로 뉴스나 글에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: With the particle -에서, common in news and written texts.

phrases.en: I'm going to meet my friend somewhere in Seoul.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때는 '모처' 대신 '어딘가'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In speech, people use 어딘가 instead of 모처.

explain_en: It is easily confused with '모처럼' (for the first time in a while), but they are different words. 모처 is used when the exact place is not revealed, as in '서울 모처', mostly in news and writing. In speech people say '어딘가'.

examples.en: I'm a member of the broadcasting club.
Ten new members joined.
All the members gathered and held a meeting.
A senior put up a poster saying they're recruiting members.
Soccer club members practice even during vacation.

examples.ko: 부원 중에 노래를 잘하는 친구가 있어요.
examples.en: Among the members there is a friend who sings well.

explain: 학교 동아리나 부서 이름에 '~부'가 붙은 곳의 구성원을 말해요. 동아리 대표는 '부장', 그 아래 사람들이 '부원'이에요. 같은 모임이어도 '회'가 붙은 곳은 '회원'이라고 해서 이름에 따라 달라요.

phrases.example: 우리 동아리는 신입 부원을 기다리고 있어요.
phrases.en: Our club is waiting for new members.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 들어온 동아리 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a person who newly joined a club.

phrases.en: The broadcasting club is recruiting members.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동아리나 부서에서 사람을 구할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a club or department is looking for people.

phrases.example: 이 독서 모임의 회원은 서른 명이에요.
phrases.en: This book club has thirty members.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이름에 '회'가 붙은 모임의 사람은 '부원'이 아니라 '회원'이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: For groups with 회 in the name, the members are 회원, not 부원.

explain_en: 부원 is a member of a group whose name ends in 부, such as a school club or department. The leader is 부장, and the others are 부원. If the group name ends in 회 instead, the member is called 회원.

examples.en: I made up my mind to start exercising this year.
He set out to tease me and started in on me.

examples.ko: 이번에는 끝까지 말하지 않기로 작정한 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems he is determined not to say anything this time.

examples.ko: 작정하면 하루에 책 한 권도 읽어요.
examples.en: When I set my mind to it, I can read a whole book in a day.

examples.ko: 아무리 작정해도 아침 일찍 일어나기는 어려워요.
examples.en: No matter how determined I am, waking up early is hard.

examples.ko: 내년에 한국에서 살기로 작정해서 한국어를 배워요.
examples.en: I've decided to live in Korea next year, so I'm learning Korean.

explain: '-기로 작정하다'나 '작정하고 + 동사'로 자주 써요. '작정하고 놀리다'처럼 일부러 마음먹고 하는 행동에는 조금 못마땅한 느낌이 섞이기도 해요. '결심하다'는 좋은 결심에 더 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: I made up my mind to go on a diet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '작정하다'와 뜻이 비슷하고 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close in meaning to '작정하다' and more natural in daily talk.

phrases.en: This time I resolved to get up early.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋은 일을 하려는 마음에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: It fits well when the resolution is for something good.

phrases.en: He spoke loudly, having made up his mind to.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미리 마음먹고 일부러 할 때 쓰고, 조금 못마땅한 느낌이 섞이기도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone does something deliberately, sometimes with a slightly disapproving tone.
phrases.en_equiv: to do on purpose, having made up one's mind

explain_en: Commonly used as -기로 작정하다 or 작정하고 + verb. In 작정하고 놀리다 (teasing on purpose), there can be a slightly disapproving tone. 결심하다 suits good resolutions better.

t90.ax: He set out to tease me and started in on me.
